# Fch

> HTTP client where the URL *is* the request. `Fch` extends the native `URL`
> class, so one object is both a mutable URL and the request that targets it,
> with retries, timeouts, dedupe, form handling and typed bodies on top. Zero
> dependencies, TypeScript, ~6.5 kB gzipped, installed from GitHub (not npm).

Key facts an agent needs before writing code:

- Install: `npm install github:westtrade/Fch#v1.13.1`. The unscoped `fch` on npm
  is a different library — never suggest it.
- Package name: `@westtrade/fch`. Subpaths: `/literal`, `/plugins/nanostores`,
  `/plugins/validate`, `/plugins/compat`.
- `fetch` is the global one unless `{ fetch }` or `setFetch()` is passed.
- Every execution (`await req`, `.json()`, `.send()`, a shortcut call, a tagged
  template) sends a NEW request. The instance is a builder, not a cached promise.
- `.json<T>()` resolves to `[data, response]`, never to the body alone.
- HTTP 4xx/5xx do NOT throw. Add `.after()` to reject, or `retries + retryOn` to
  retry them.
- A tagged template starts immediately, so `setRetries()`/`setTimeout()` after it
  are too late. Use the class or a client when configuration is needed.

## Three spellings of the same request

```ts
import { Fch } from "@westtrade/fch";
const [u] = await new Fch("https://api.test/u/1").json<User>();     // class

import { fch } from "@westtrade/fch";
const api = fch.create({ baseUrl: "https://api.test", timeout: 5000 });
const [u] = await api.get<User>("/u/1");                            // client

import fch from "@westtrade/fch/literal";
const [u] = await fch.get<User>`https://api.test/u/1`;              // tagged template
```

## Common tasks — minimal code

```ts
// GET JSON, typed
const [user] = await fch.get<User>`https://api.test/users/1`;

// POST JSON (object -> JSON + Content-Type)
fch.post({ name: "Ann" })`https://api.test/users`;

// other body encodings: a string in the options slot, or options.encode
api.post("/users", body, "urlencoded");                    // x-www-form-urlencoded
api.post("/users", body, { encode: "form", retries: 2 });  // multipart

// query params: the instance IS a URL
const req = new Fch("https://api.test/search");
req.searchParams.set("q", "Tom & Jerry");   // encoded correctly
const [hits] = await req.json<Hit[]>();

// retries + timeout + retry policy (configure before the request starts)
await new Fch(url, {
  retries: 3, retryDelay: 500, maxRetryDelay: 10_000, timeout: 5000,
  retryOn: (res) => !!res && (res.status === 429 || res.status >= 500),
}).json();

// reject on HTTP errors
const httpError = (res: Response) => { if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`); return res; };
await api.request("/users/1").after(httpError).json<User>();

// cancel (the builder stays reusable)
const r = new Fch(url, { retries: 5 }); const p = r.send(); r.abort(); await p.catch(() => {});

// forms: a <form>, a submit Event, FormData, or a CSS selector
api.post("/houses", e);                  // submit event
req.setFormData("#checkout");            // selector
await req.setFormData(form).send();      // element

// dedupe concurrent GETs
const shared = new Fch(url, { dedupe: true });
await Promise.all([shared.json(), shared.json()]);  // 1 request on the wire

// polling: an async generator; every iteration is a NEW request, and a failure
// is yielded (not thrown) so the loop survives it. It owns its stop signal, so
// it survives an earlier abort(); req.abort() still stops a running poll.
for await (const res of new Fch(url).poll(1000, controller)) {
  if (res instanceof Error) continue;
  if ((await res.json()).done) break;
}

// per-call options without a chain
await api.request("/houses/1", { retries: 5 }).json<House>();

// write with idempotency
await new Fch(url, { method: "POST", dedupe: true, dedupeKey: () => crypto.randomUUID() })
  .setJsonBody(order).send();
```

## Plugins

```ts
// store: the request becomes a NanoStore (useStore works in any framework)
const req = new Fch(url).use(nanostores());
req.get();          // { loading, data, error, timer, delayed, timedOut, response }
await req.json();

// validation: 'formData' (the DEFAULT) checks before sending, 'response' after.
// A bare validate(rules) means 'formData'; attach both with two use() calls.
// Note: formData skips a JSON body (logged as a warning), it does not fail.
new Fch(url)
  .use(validate("formData", { schema: { type: "object", required: ["name"] } }))
  .use(validate("response", { schema: { type: "object", required: ["id"] } }))
  .json();

// logging (core only emits events; the plugin prints)
new Fch(url).use(logger({ debug: true }));

// custom deprecated aliases (not in core)
new Fch(url).use(compat()).setRetryTimeout(500);
```

## Loading timers

`idle -> submitting -> delayed -> timeout`, with `delayMs` (500) and `timeoutMs`
(8000). They are observational and never abort; `timeout` is what aborts.

```ts
const req = new Fch(url, { delayMs: 500, timeoutMs: 8000 });
req.delayed;  // getter in plain Fch; a store key with the nanostores plugin
```

## Docs

Start here:

- [Getting started](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/getting-started.html): install, first request, mental model
- [Why not plain fetch](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/vs-fetch.html): what fetch makes you write yourself
- [How Fch compares](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/vs-libraries.html): axios, ky, ofetch, wretch, with sizes

Core ideas:

- [The URL is the request](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/url-first.html): why one object instead of two
- [Bodies, headers, methods](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/requests.html): JSON, forms, binary, auth
- [Reading responses](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/reading-responses.html): tuples, typed JSON, when to throw

Reliability:

- [Retries & backoff](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/retries.html): exponential, jittered, abort-aware
- [Timeouts](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/timeouts.html): per attempt, `timeout` vs `timeoutMs`
- [Deduplication](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/dedupe.html): one request on the wire
- [Cancelling](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/cancelling.html): abort and keep the builder
- [Polling](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/polling.html): repeat a request, and when not to

Working with DOM:

- [Forms & events](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/forms.html): a `<form>`, an event, or a selector
- [Shorthand API](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/shortcuts.html): `api.get` / `post`, per-call options
- [Tagged template](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/literal.html): `fch\`https://…\``, `withFetch`, `raw`

Extending and operating:

- [Plugins](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/plugins.html): the plugin contract, first-party list
- [Nano Stores](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/nanostores.html): store integration, form examples per framework
- [Validation](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/validate.html): schema or custom validator
- [Interceptors](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/hooks.html): `before()` / `after()`
- [Logging](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/logging.html): pluggable logger, quiet by default
- [API reference](https://westtrade.github.io/Fch/docs/api.html): every method and option
